title: HLA-B*15:02 / carbamazepine SJS/TEN risk: actionable but ancestry-scoped pharmacogenomic control
summary: Positive-control record for MKH-PAT-0015 and scope-control record for MKH-PAT-0016. It shows that some gene-drug associations are clinically actionable, but also that actionability is population-scoped, imperfect, and not deterministic.

status_history.note: Promoted after rev0019 asked for further negative-control/counterexample and ancestry/diversity caveat work.

place.scope: carbamazepine prescribing label; genetic-risk populations; no patient-level guidance

claims.claim: The DailyMed carbamazepine label warns about serious and sometimes fatal dermatologic reactions including SJS/TEN, states that studies in patients of Chinese ancestry found a strong association between SJS/TEN risk and HLA-B*1502, and says genetically at-risk patients should be screened before carbamazepine initiation.
what_would_change_status: A materially updated FDA/DailyMed label changes the HLA-B*1502 screening or avoidance language.

claims.claim: The same label makes population scope part of the evidence object: HLA-B*1502 prevalence varies across Asian populations, is reported as lower in Japan and Korea, is largely absent in individuals not of Asian origin, and screening decisions are cautioned by variability within ethnic groups, difficulty ascertaining ancestry, and mixed ancestry.
what_would_change_status: A newer label or guideline replaces this population-scope framing with a materially different genetic-screening policy.

claims.claim: This control is not deterministic: the label says HLA-B*1502 genotyping has important limitations, must not substitute for clinical vigilance, many positive Asian patients will not develop SJS/TEN, and reactions can still occur infrequently in negative patients of any ethnicity.
what_would_change_status: A later authoritative label or guideline removes the non-determinism/vigilance caveat.

evidence_profile.why_control_not_case: It is not a negative result; it is a robust/actionable pharmacogenomic contrast with explicit population and clinical-vigilance limits.

type_payload.fit_rationale: A strong and actionable gene-drug relation that still requires ancestry/population and clinical-vigilance qualifiers; prevents both anti-genetics overfit and naive universal transfer.
limits: No individual-level prescribing recommendation is made.
The label is one product/label surface, not a full CPIC/FDA/clinical-guideline review.
Uses ancestry descriptors as label language while flagging mixed ancestry and descriptor limits.

handling_notes: No clinical advice; use only as an epistemic/actionability-control record.
Avoid treating ancestry labels as biological essences; preserve label caveats about mixed ancestry and within-group variability.

unknowns: No historical adoption/utilization curve for HLA-B*15:02 screening is encoded.
No ancestry-descriptor ethics review beyond label caveat is complete.
next_actions: Add implementation/practice-lag child record if utilization data is source-acquired.
Compare with HLA-B*5701/abacavir to split pharmacogenomic controls by phenotype, drug, and population scope.

scope_qualifiers.ancestry_or_population_scope: genetically at-risk populations with label caveats about mixed ancestry and within-group variability
scope_qualifiers.portability_caution: screening has limitations and is not deterministic
